text: Over the natural numbers with R(x, y) meaning 'x < y', which of the following is correct?
choices: ∃y ∀x (x < y) is true; ∀x ∃y (x < y) is false
∀x ∃y (x < y) is true; ∃y ∀x (x < y) is false
explanation: ∀x ∃y (x < y) is true (given n, take the witness y = n+1). ∃y ∀x (x < y) is false (no natural number exceeds every natural number). The valid implication runs ∃y∀x ⟹ ∀x∃y, never the reverse, so options 1, 2, and 3 mis-evaluate at least one sentence.
